text:
amy: evening slice window at 21:00 PT, 45m. quick rollcall and freeze exceptions?

ryan: here. prepping a staggered canary. pinned runtime image to rwinf/runtime:v2026-03-21-1

qa: smoke checklist posted in the thread below. main items: p95 < 90ms, error-rate < 0.15%, tail-sample checks for long-context cases

sofia: note: this release touches kernel scheduling. NO API changes. we'd prefer no hotfixes in the slice unless critical. please declare any exemptions now

deploy-bot: starting canary -> service: inference-edge-pool, targets: 4 hosts, policy: gradual, step=2 hosts, health-check=smoke-suite

ryan: config for canary: concurrency=16, batch_window_ms=8, kv_cache=warm-start

ops-oncall: i'll bump alert windows to 3x baseline for latency and set an emergency rollback trigger if errors > 0.6% sustained for 3m

qa: running quick regression harness now:
```bash
./tools/regress.sh --suite smoke --target inference-edge-pool --duration 90 --qps 20
```

deploy-bot: canary progress 50% -> 2/4 hosts updated. smoke-suite OK on updated hosts. no infra alerts

amy: FYI billing-team requested we watch embedding-token-rate for the next 6h; tagging it in release notes as 'monitor'

qa: one transient 504 on host-2 during heavy long-context test. stack trace shows http_proxy timeout in fronting layer

ryan: pulling logs from host-2, looks like socket backlog brief spike. increasing upstream timeout to 10s for this canary step

sofia: decision: continue but pause further steps if same 504 repeats twice in 5m. ops-oncall you have rollback authority if it crosses the threshold

ops-oncall: acknowledged. rollback cmd in playbook: deploy rollback --svc inference-edge-pool --to v2026-03-19-stable --reason '504 spike on canary'

deploy-bot: canary step complete -> 4/4 hosts updated. smoke pass. no sustained errors.

amy: short release-note: kernel scheduler tweaks for long prompts, p99 improvement expected, watch embedding-token-rate. no surface API change.

sofia: once billing and prod dashboards look green after 30m we finish rollout. please log any followups as postmortem if needed. thanks :sparkles:
